title: Exact completion functor and its canonical triangle comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with uniformizer $\pi$, and $X$ any scheme. Work in $D(R)$ for $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, with the coefficient category of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] and localization $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an unbounded complex $M$ take the strict reduction tower $D_\bullet(M)$, its transitions and maps $j_n$ of [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus], and apply the Roos functor $H$ of [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]. The formula $F(QM)=QH(D_\bullet(M))$ descends to an additive endofunctor $F:D(R)\to D(R)$, and
$$c_M(m)=(((m,0))_{n\ge1},0)$$
descends to a natural transformation $c:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow F$ which is the canonical completion map of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] up to isomorphism: for every $K\in D(R)$ there is an isomorphism from $F(K)$ to the derived limit $R\varprojlim_nK_n$ specified there, under which $c_K$ corresponds to the specified canonical map $K\to R\varprojlim_nK_n$. In particular $K$ is derived complete if and only if $c_K$ is an isomorphism. There are coherent natural comparisons $\sigma_{K,r}:F(K[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(K)[r]$ for all $r\in\mathbf Z$, satisfying $\sigma_{K,r}c_{K[r]}=c_K[r]$. For every distinguished triangle $T=(K\xrightarrow{f}L\to C\xrightarrow{w}K[1])$, its image $F(T)$, whose last arrow is $\sigma_{K,1}F(w)$, is distinguished, and $(c_K,c_L,c_C):T\to F(T)$ is a morphism of triangles, including its last square with $c_K[1]$.
